summary: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company, LLC is an American company that operates the luxury Ritz-Carlton hotel chain, which has 91 hotels and resorts in 30 countries and territories. The note describes its 1998 ownership changes: Blackstone Real Estate Acquisitions bought The Ritz-Carlton Boston at auction, then Marriott International acquired that hotel and later bought the Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co. and worldwide name rights from W.B. Johnson.
one_line: Overview of The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company, its luxury hotel chain, and its 1998 sale to Marriott International.
key_facts: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company, LLC is an American company that operates the luxury hotel chain known as The Ritz-Carlton.
The Ritz-Carlton has 91 luxury hotels and resorts in 30 countries and territories.
Blackstone Real Estate Acquisitions of New York bought The Ritz-Carlton Boston at auction for $75 million in February 1998.
A month after its purchase, Marriott International of Bethesda, Maryland, acquired The Ritz-Carlton Boston from Blackstone for $100 million.
Marriott franchises and manages Marriott's 325,000 rooms, according to the note.
Marriott International bought The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co. and rights to The Ritz-Carlton name worldwide from W.B. Johnson.
Marriott's purchase of The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co. and worldwide name rights from W.B. Johnson was valued at $290 million.
The $290 million Marriott transaction was a two-part transaction completed in 1998.
